item.title: Goalie Parker Gahagen shares his unique path that led him to Railers
item.description: He played two seasons of hockey in Florida. He nearly played hardball there as well. Parker Gahagen was his baseball team’s MVP in 2011 while at Williamsville North High School, located 12 miles northeast of Buffalo, New York. And he seriously considered playing at Florida Southern, which has won nine Division 2 national championships and produced 13 Major Leaguers. Currently in his 10 th professional hockey season – spanning 13 teams – the Worcester Railers goalie has no regrets concerning his career choice. The man with 122 career pro wins is still connected to baseball, however. Mostly from afar, but also through his dog. Gahagen follows a certain team that wears pinstripes - “My dad is a Yankees fans, so it carried down,” he said – and his corgi is named Yogi Berra. Berra, as she is known, ran in the annual Buffalo Bills Corgi Cup championship at Highmark Stadium on Sept. 27 at halftime of the Bills/Rams game, competing against the likes of Fenway Frank, Sauerkraut Kenobi and Riot. “She didn’t win; she got distracted,” Gahagen said. “But she had the most fun out there.” She also has 484 followers @berrathecorgi on Instagram. In an interview held at Worcester Ice Center on the eve of the World Series, Gahagen also picked the Milwaukee Brewers to win the World Series. “I feel like they might deserve it a little bit more,” he said. “I like how they play small ball. All the finer details. It’d be cool to see that type of team win. Usually, it’s always about the long ball.” (The Brewers clinched the Series in five games Wednesday night, hitting just three home runs). Back to hockey. Gahagen has played on the West Coast (San Jose Barricuda), the Rockies (Utah Grizzlies; Colorado Eagles), the Northeast United States (Lehigh Valley Phantoms; Reading Royals) and in Canada. While he won the Kelly Cup with the Florida Everblades in 2022, another unforgettable memory happened well to the north when he played for the Newfoundland Growlers in '19-20. Gahagen won 10 of the 15 games he played and posted a career-low 1.81 goals against average, but what happened outside the rink has never left him. “We got snowed in to our apartments for week and half,” he said. “The snow was above the door frames; that one’s hard to forget. item.title: Andoni Iraola reacts to Liverpool’s Carabap Cup quarter-final draw
item.description: Andoni Iraola reacts to Liverpool’s Carabap Cup quarter-final draw Andoni Iraola Draws Bournemouth as Liverpool Eye Carabao Cup Semi-Finals Liverpool are through to the Carabao Cup quarter-finals, and Andoni Iraola got the one draw he plainly did not want. After beating Chelsea on penalties and watching Bournemouth knock out Aston Villa, Liverpool were paired with the south coast club in the last eight. That gives Iraola another meeting with a club he knows inside out. He has already faced Bournemouth once this season, when Liverpool won 1-0 at the Vitality Stadium in September. Now comes a second reunion, this time at Anfield, with a place in the semi-finals on the line. The Liverpool head coach did not pretend otherwise when asked about the draw. He said, “Honestly, I was talking before the draw and I said, ‘The only team I don’t want is Bournemouth…’ For me, it’s special. They know me very well, they are playing very well lately, in a good moment, but it is what it is. “We haven’t been very lucky with the draws, we have played Spurs and Chelsea already and now Bournemouth. That is going to be obviously special for me, but we have to earn the right to be in the semi-finals and I hope we can do it here at home again.” That sums it up well enough. Sentiment matters for about five minutes. Then it becomes a football problem. Liverpool do at least have the obvious advantage of playing at Anfield. In cup ties like this, that matters. So does momentum, and there is plenty of that around this competition now. With Arsenal, Chelsea, Tottenham and Manchester United already out, the bracket looks lighter than it did a few weeks ago. Nobody will hand Liverpool a route to Wembley, but the path is there. Photo: IMAGO Carabao Cup Draw Gives Liverpool a Real Opening This is why Iraola has treated the competition seriously from the start. Domestic cups are often dressed up as distractions until the draw opens up. Then everybody suddenly remembers that silverware still counts, and that a semi-final is one round away. Bournemouth will not arrive as obliging visitors. Back in September, they were still looking for traction under Marco Rose. That has changed quickly. Results have improved, confidence has followed, and they have shown they can punish good sides when given space and rhythm. Bournemouth Threat Makes Quarter-Final Complicated For Liverpool, this tie is awkward for personal reasons and dangerous for football reasons. Bournemouth know Iraola, and Iraola knows them. That usually strips away some of the surprise and leaves a game to be decided by execution, control and nerve. Still, this is the kind of tie Liverpool should want. It is at home, it is winnable, and it brings a genuine chance of reaching the last four of the Carabao Cup. Iraola may not have asked for Bournemouth, but he has been handed an opportunity. He would be foolish to complain too much about that. Further details of the draw and scheduling have been reported here.

More than a week after the controversy, Trump found an unlikely ally in Charles Barkley. While Barkley made clear he doesn't pay any mind to what Trump says, he sided with the president in thinking James' approach to the anthem was inappropriate. Here's a look at what Barkley said. MORE: Ranking the impact of NBA early-season injuries Charles Barkley says LeBron James was 'disrespectful' during national anthem Barkley explained in an appearance on SiriusXM NBA Radio why he wouldn't do what James did during the national anthem. Barkley explained that while he believes anyone should be allowed to protest during the national anthem, he "always" stands for the anthem because of American values like freedom of speech and his respect for military members, "I always stand for the anthem. I just think it's important," Barkley said. "We live in the greatest country ever. item.description: PISCATAWAY - Most freshmen wrestlers would look at a weight as loaded as the NCAA 125-pound class is and temper their expectations. It's deep waters but Rutgers University freshman Anthony Knox does not fret about it. He has never lacked for confidence in his own abilites, and for good reason. He is one of five wrestlers to win four NJSIAA championships on the mat. "It's not an excuse that I'm a freshman. The time to win is now.'' Penn State's Luke Lilledahl, the defending national champion, heads the weight class. Also at 125 is Nebraska's Vincent Robinson, the 2025 national champion when he was at North Carolina State; Princeton's Marc-Anthony McGowan, the runner-up last season; and Oklahoma State's Troy Spratley, the 2025 runner-up. And those four are just for starters. Stanford's Nico Provo, third last year, Minnesota's Jore Volk and Virginia Tech's Eddie Ventresca are among the other past All-Americans at the weight. item.title: SA vs AUS: Josh Inglis becomes first Australian cricketer to achieve this rare feat in all three formats
item.description: Josh Inglis etched his name into Australian cricket history with a second Test century before Australia were bowled out for 429 on Day 3 of the series-deciding third Test against South Africa at Newlands on Thursday. The visitors secured a crucial 100-run first-innings lead after dismissing the hosts for 329. Inglis scored 102 off 135 balls, including 11 fours and two sixes, to become the first Australian batter to register at least two centuries in each of the three international formats. His landmark knock came on his return to the Test side after nearly a year away from the format and helped Australia build a significant advantage in the series decider. The wicketkeeper-batter reached his century with a reverse sweep against off-spinner Simon Harmer before eventually falling to the same bowler. His innings, combined with Alex Carey's 80, proved instrumental in taking Australia past South Africa's first-innings total. Inglis becomes first Australian with multiple centuries in all three formats Inglis's achievement places him in a unique category in Australian cricket. He now has two centuries each in Tests, ODIs and T20Is, becoming the first Australian batter to reach the milestone across all three formats. His maiden Test century came against Sri Lanka in 2025. He has also registered two ODI hundreds and two T20I centuries, underlining his ability to make an impact across formats. The numbers highlight the significance of his achievement: Tests: 286 runs in six matches, with a highest score of 102, an average of 35.75 and two centuries. ODIs: 1,100 runs in 43 matches, with a highest score of 120 not out, an average of 30.55 and two centuries. T20Is: 1,033 runs in 49 matches, with a highest score of 110, an average of 26.48 and two centuries. Only three Australian batters have scored multiple T20I centuries: Inglis, Glenn Maxwell and Aaron Finch. However, neither Maxwell nor Finch has managed at least two hundreds in all three formats. Maxwell has five T20I centuries and four ODI hundreds, but only one Test ton, scored against India in 2017. Finch, meanwhile, finished his international career with 17 ODI centuries and two T20I hundreds but never scored a Test century. Inglis is now the only Australian batter to have multiple centuries in each format. Inglis makes Test comeback count Inglis returned to Australia's playing XI for the series decider after recovering from a fractured finger sustained during the preceding ODI series against South Africa. He had last played a Test during the 2025 Ashes at home. Australia made four changes to their side for the Newlands Test, bringing Inglis back alongside Cameron Green, Nathan Lyon and Cooper Connolly. South Africa had earlier posted 329 in their first innings, putting the onus on Australia's batters to build a substantial response. item.title: Was the Kings’ First Win a Turning Point or a Temporary Reprieve?
item.description: The Los Angeles Kings finally secured their first win of the season against the Washington Capitals on Oct. 20. Since then, however, their results have been mixed, leaving questions about whether the team has genuinely turned a corner or simply enjoyed a brief reprieve. The Kings have gone 2-2 in their four games since beating Washington. They followed that victory with a 3-2 overtime win over the New York Islanders before losing 3-1 to the New Jersey Devils. A convincing 6-3 win over the New York Rangers offered further encouragement, but a 2-1 loss to the Chicago Blackhawks brought them back down to earth. View this post on Instagram Panarin Leads the Kings’ Offense Artemi Panarin has been a key contributor during the Kings’ recent stretch, recording four points across the past four games. His offensive production has helped Los Angeles win, though the team still needs more consistency across its forward group. Alex Laferriere has also made an impact, recording three points over the same span. He collected an assist against the Islanders and added two more against the Rangers, providing valuable secondary scoring. These contributions are encouraging, but the Kings cannot afford to rely on a handful of players to carry the offense. Sustained success will require more consistent production across the lineup, especially when their leading scorers can’t take over. Clarke Provides a Blue-Line Boost Brandt Clarke has emerged as another bright spot, recording three points in the four-game stretch, including two goals and an assist. His offensive contributions give Los Angeles another avenue to generate scoring chances beyond its forwards. item.title: Scottish football could pave way for 3pm TV blackout to end
item.description: Games currently cannot be shown live between 2:45pm and 5:15pm on a Saturday [Getty Images] The first tentative steps to end the 3pm television blackout in the UK have been taken by Scottish football as it seeks offers for the next broadcast cycle. The SPFL has said that it is "flexible about the number of games" that will form part of the new deal, which will kick in from the 2029-30 season. BBC Sport understands this includes the possibility that broadcasters could bid to show all matches live - including those shown on a Saturday afternoon. The SPFL has created a tender with the greatest flexibility on the basis that the broadcaster does not seek to impose Article 48 of the Uefa Statutes. Article 48 allows leagues to set specific times when matches are banned from being shown live on television. It can only be enforced when 50% of matches in a country's top two divisions are played at the same time. While other parts of Europe have experimented with a blackout, it is now only present in the UK between 2:45pm and 5:15pm on a Saturday. Other leagues now tend to stagger kick-off times so the top divisions do not all play at the same time, meaning the blackout could not be applied. In the UK, 3pm remains the traditional, default kick-off time for all leagues from the very top down through non-league. It was introduced due to fears that televised games at 3pm could affect attendances, not just at the clubs involved but at those down the divisions too. But as streaming has grown in popularity, critics have argued that it hinders the ability of clubs to exploit this revenue stream. This is especially the case in the lower levels, which have had to adhere to the blackout and not show any of their games online. In August, Premier League chief executive Richard Masters indicated the direction of travel was to end the blackout, but any decision would be 18 months away and taken in consultation with the EFL and the FA. The upcoming broadcast cycle provides a unique opportunity for all leagues to come together and reach a consensus, as the rights deals for the Premier League, EFL and SPFL all end in 2028-29. While the possibility to take all games is on the table in Scotland, it is by no means certain the option will be taken up. Under the current terms, Sky Sports can show up to 60 Premiership matches a season, with Premier Sports showing up to 22. In total, there are 228 games in the top flight, meaning only 36% of matches are shown live under the current broadcast deal. The tender allows broadcasters to present any proposition for live coverage they see fit. Any decision would then be up to the Premiership's 12 member clubs, with eight votes required to approve a deal. Clubs could potentially opt to reject an offer which would include the Saturday 3pm games. Scotland ending the 3pm blackout would not automatically mean English, Welsh and Northern Irish football follows suit.

item.title: How Devin Vassell's 'extremely mature performance' helped save Spurs in Utah
item.description: San Antonio Spurs guard Devin Vassell (24) goes for a layup against Utah Jazz guard Ace Bailey (19) during the first half of an NBA basketball game, Wednesday, Oct. 28, 2026, in Salt Lake City. (Rob Gray/AP Photo/Rob Gray) SALT LAKE CITY - The Spurs' decisive 12-0 run in overtime of Wednesday night's 117-111 victory over Utah had Devin Vassell's fingerprints all over it. After Brice Sensabaugh got things started in the extra session with a 3-pointer that gave the Jazz a 108-105 lead, Vassell responded with a 10-foot jumper in the lane. One minute later, his two-handed follow slam after Josh Green blocked Dylan Harper's layup attempt gave the Spurs a 111-108 lead. Thirty-five seconds later, Vassell fed Victor Wembanyama with a long lob pass that resulted in an easy bucket for a seven-point cushion. "He was tremendous, especially coming down the stretch," Spurs forward Keldon Johnson said of Vassell. "He got some nice buckets. Some big rebounds. He made some big shots, made great decisions. He did everything we needed for him to do to get the win." That included his Johnny-on-the-spot put back after the block on Harper. item.title: Man United risk missing out on Julian Nagelsmann as two European clubs complicate pursuit
item.description: Man United risk missing out on Julian Nagelsmann as two European clubs complicate pursuit Manchester United’s interest are at risk of missing out on the services of former Germany boss Julian Nagelsmann, following major developments involving RB Leipzig and Fenerbahce. Nagelsmann interest Nagelsmann is believed to be of interest to United amidst uncertainty over Michael Carrick’s future. Carrick is facing a major battle to keep his job as United endure a miserable start to the season. United have now gone eight games without a victory; last weekend’s 3-0 humbling to Bournemouth was the latest episode of their woeful run. After the match against Bournemouth, it was overwhelmingly anticipated that Carrick would be sacked, and his lap of honour around Old Trafford strongly indicated a farewell. But after lengthy deliberations, club chiefs opted to retain him. Carrick will be in charge for Saturday’s clash against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge. A report covered by The Peoples Person relayed that United are disinclined to pay the compensation fee to part ways with Carrick, while they also remain uncertain about the suitability of his potential replacements. Nagelsmann has admirers at United, chiefly director of recruitment Christopher Vivell. It’s understood Vivell is pushing hard for the club to appoint Nagelsmann, while director of football Jason Wilcox is advocating for Eddie Howe. Nagelsmann would listen to United’s pitch as he eyes a return to football management after he was dismissed by Germany. But if United want Nagelsmann, they may need to move fast. According to BILD [via SportWitness ], Leipzig want Nagelsmann. The 39-year-old is also of interest to Fenerbahce. Nagelsmann threat The report claims that Leipzig have Nagelsmann firmly in their sights if they decide to pull the trigger and sack Martin Demichelis. Like Carrick, Demichelis is struggling and if he fails to turn the situation around, Leipzig will sanction a change in the dugout. Nagelsmann is Leipzig’s top choice to replace Demichelis. The Bundesliga outfit are aware that Nagelsmann is on the radar of United and Tottenham Hotspur. Meanwhile, Hurriyet say that Fenerbahce president Aziz Yildirim wants a foreign coach to come in for Ismail Kartal, who was recently let go. Yildirim has two options in mind: Vincenzo Montella and Nagelsmann. Fenerbahce will initiate contact soon to gauge availability.

item.title: Why this Eagles trade candidate could land with the Steelers
item.description: Stuck in a five-game losing streak, the Philadelphia Eagles could be serious sellers at the NFL trade deadline — and one name keeps popping up. Eagles cornerback Riq Woolen is considered one of the most obvious trade candidates, if not the most obvious, on the roster as this season has continued to spiral. And there’s a chance the Eagles send him across the state to the Pittsburgh Steelers. We acknowledged Woolen as a trade chip if the Eagles keep losing as the Nov. 10 deadline nears. And on Wednesday, ESPN also acknowledged Woolen could be on the move. ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler and Matt Bowen ranked the NFL’s top 25 trade candidates with the deadline looming. Woolen came in at No. 8, the highest of any Eagles player. “When I talk to rival teams about which players Philly might move,” Fowler wrote, “Woolen’s name comes up fairly often.” Woolen made it clear on Wednesday that he doesn’t pay much attention to his name being mentioned in trade rumors. He dealt with it last year when he was with the Seahawks, too. #Eagles CB Riq Woolen on trade rumors: “I’m here in Philly, where I want to be” pic.twitter.com/QakLMGL1HT — Johnny McGonigal (@jmcgonigal9) October 28, 2026 “Y’all can say a million things, but y’all wouldn’t really know until you get a talk with the GM and you get a talk with your coach,” Woolen said. “You can see me going to any team or hear anything about any team. But to me, that doesn’t matter to me. Just because I’m here working with these guys. ... My brothers need me. They don’t need my mind to be anywhere else. That’s my job being here. “In Philly, I worked my butt off all offseason. So I’m going to ride with these guys throughout this season whether we’re undefeated or we don’t win a game. I’ll work my butt off with them, and they work hard as hell, too. I’m going to be where my feet are at and let the chips fall where they may.” But the reality of the situation is, Woolen’s feet may be in a different team’s locker room in a week or two. It’s apparent why that’s the case. Woolen is on an expiring contract. He’s a volatile player; he’s been mostly good this season before being torched in Monday’s loss to Dallas. And his $1.26 million base salary is easy for a team to stomach. But where could he go? ESPN listed three potential teams as fits for Woolen: the Detroit Lions, Carolina Panthers and Steelers. The Steelers are thin at cornerback after dealing Joey Porter Jr. to the Cowboys. Woolen could make sense there. The Panthers and Lions have injuries at cornerback, too. But there’s a pre-existing relationship between Eagles GM Howie Roseman and Steelers assistant GM Andy Weidl, who was in the Eagles’ front office from 2016-22. If Woolen is dealt, Roseman will likely be looking for a fourth-round or fifth-round pick for him. ESPN is predicting that there’s a 35% chance Woolen is dealt. item.description: Will the roof be open or closed when Georgia faces Florida at Mercedes-Benz Stadium this weekend? The Southeastern Conference says it has no policy requiring either option for the game. In an email, the SEC said the conference does not have a policy determining whether the stadium's roof must be open or closed for SEC games at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. "There is not an SEC policy that would determine whether the roof is open or closed for SEC games at MBS," the SEC noted. They added that the conference office chooses to close the roof for the SEC Championship Game in December, but said that practice does not establish a policy for this weekend's matchup. It was also noted that the teams will work with Mercedes-Benz Stadium to determine if it will be open or closed. The stadium's roof status for Saturday's game had not been confirmed at the time of publication. "We're playing in Atlanta this year. What does that change? It doesn't," Kirby Smart said during the summer. "Let's be honest, just the venue we are playing in will be different. "Sometimes down there wind is a big factor, heat. Going to be indoors in an incredible stadium and venue that we've gotten play in multiple times." When is the Georgia-Florida game? Georgia and Florida are scheduled to meet Saturday, Oct. 31, at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta for the Invesco QQQ Atlanta Gridiron Classic. According to the University of Georgia Athletics website, kickoff is scheduled for 3:30 p.m. EDT. Stadium gates are scheduled to open at 2 p.m., according to the venue’s event page. The game is being played in Atlanta while renovations continue at Jacksonville's EverBank Stadium, where the rivalry has traditionally been held. item.title: Paul Heyman Sums up Vince McMahon in One Word, And It’s Perfect
item.description: USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Connect Paul Heyman has worked closely with both of the men who have run WWE creative over the past two decades, and he says the two experiences have been completely different. During an interview on In Depth with Graham Bensinger , Heyman described Vince McMahon as a “dictator” who saw WWE as his show and contrasted him with Triple H , whose real name is Paul Levesque. “Well, Paul runs the creative. And it’s a much different environment with Paul running the creative than Vince, because they are distinctly different personalities. Vince was a dictator. It was his money, and therefore it’s his show. And you’re going to be the executive director, or you’re going to be the lead writer, or you’re going to be my top idea man,” Heyman said. Heyman explained that pitching an idea to McMahon meant trying to talk him out of a vision he already had in his head. He did an impression of McMahon to describe how those conversations went. “‘Graham, I see this is not half empty, it’s not half full. That is a percentage which I have in my mind, and you can’t talk me out of it.’ ‘Well, Vince, what’s in your mind?’ ‘I don’t know. Why don’t you tell me what’s in your mind, and talk me out of what’s in mine?” Heyman said. WWE “So, you better be good at pitching. And it’s the constant chase for Vince to buy into your ideas over his own. That’s the dynamic of pitching Vince McMahon. He’s right, he has the right to be wrong. It’s his show; give me your best shot. “Because if you can sell Vince, you can sell the talent, you can sell the lieutenants, and you can sell the audience. So if you’re that good of a salesman, he’s going to buy it. And then it’s his idea because he gets the credit, because he’s the owner.” Heyman said the process works very differently under Triple H. “That’s not the way it works today. Paul Levesque is not a dictator; he’s a collaborator. See, Vince loves a blank piece of paper. Paul Levesque doesn’t like the blank piece of paper. He accepts the fact that the paper has writing on it already. He’s the best editor I’ve ever worked with in my entire life, ever,” Heyman said. “Because he’s an open collaborator that walks in the room with no expectations of his own vision. His vision is to listen to very smart people that have different ideas than he does. So, he’s a collaborator the likes of which I’ve never had the pleasure of working with. It’s just a completely different experience.” Triple H took over WWE creative in July 2022 after McMahon retired. McMahon later resigned from TKO, WWE’s parent company, in January 2024.
